taxonomic_note: Older Texas records placed multiple entities under Symphyotrichum subulatum. Modern Texas treatment separates former var. ligulatum as Symphyotrichum divaricatum and former var. parviflorum as Symphyotrichum expansum; true S. subulatum is concentrated in far southeast Texas.
look_here_first: TRUE eastern annual saltmarsh aster under the narrow modern Texas concept: first photograph the ENTIRE flowering array on an unmowed mature plant. S. subulatum typically concentrates more heads in an upper, denser PYRAMID, whereas inland S. divaricatum is conspicuously DIFFUSE with large gaps between flower heads. The denser pyramid is relative, not a solid cone; mowed or damaged plants and single head macros cannot establish the split. Check narrow sessile leaves, side-view phyllaries (green zone towards distal part of bracts reported for subulatum, overlap/visibility uncertain), and coastal or saline SE Texas provenance; do NOT use habitat alone. The older Uvalde 'S. subulatum' image is quarantined as taxonomically incompatible without independent review.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Current Texas taxonomic treatment places true Symphyotrichum subulatum in the far southeastern part of the state rather than the Central Texas project zone. The Purola Hays record reflects the older broad subulatum concept and is not used as current-species evidence.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Historical var. ligulatum records in Central Texas must not be counted as true S. subulatum; they map to S. divaricatum.

best_field_traits: many small heads in relatively dense pyramidal inflorescence
small pale lavender to whitish rays
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use whole unmowed terminal array and phyllary side view. S. subulatum more top-dense pyramidal, saline/coastal SE Texas; S. divaricatum open diffuse with widely separated heads and common inland. The green portion of phyllaries is reported upper-only in subulatum vs extending farther down in divaricatum, but hard to see reliably; never force from one fuzzy bract photo. Prior Uvalde 2014 label is OLD/BROAD or unresolved concept and does NOT certify current true subulatum.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. divaricatum widely spaced heads/loosely diffuse inflorescence, usually inland non-saline habitat; TRUE S. subulatum more compact upper pyramid, largely coastal saline SE Texas. The morphology overlaps, especially after mowing. Historical subulatum var. ligulatum now goes to S. divaricatum in project; var. parviflorum historically to S. expansum. Quarantined Uvalde Commons photo is NOT species identity proof.
